changes_vs_current: New topic. Raw order by average position over 5 people sources (YouGov Ratings popularity, YouGov Ratings fame, YouGov BrandIndex consideration 2024, same 2025, company revenue): 1 Nike 2.8, 2 Adidas 3.8, 3 Levi's 5.0, 4 Skechers 6.8, 5 Old Navy 7.8, 6 Hanes 10.6, 7 Under Armour 11.6, 8 Fruit of the Loom 11.6, 9 Victoria's Secret 12.2, 10 Puma 13.8, 11 New Balance 14.4, 12 Calvin Klein 14.8, 13 Louis Vuitton 15.4, 14 Wrangler 15.8, 15 Gap 15.8, 16 The North Face 15.8, 17 Ralph Lauren 16.4, 18 Converse 16.8, 19 Reebok 16.8, 20 Gucci 17.4, 21 Tommy Hilfiger 18.2, 22 Banana Republic 19.2, 23 Vans 19.6, 24 Lee 19.8, 25 American Eagle 20.6, 26 Crocs 20.6, 27 H&M 20.8. Gut-check moves (sources are opinion/consideration/awareness/sales, none is free recall of 'clothing brands', and none puts these gut picks low on recall grounds): Gap 15->7 (revenue #9 with Old Navy, fame 92%; quintessential clothing brand); Ralph Lauren 17->8 (Polo RL 59% popularity, revenue #14; 'Polo' is a top recall answer); Calvin Klein 12->9 (fame 96%, revenue #13); Tommy Hilfiger 21->12 (fame 94%, revenue #13 via PVH); American Eagle 25->13 (fame 91%, revenue #19; top jeans search brand); H&M 27->15 (revenue #5, largest store-brand by sales in the US set). Judgment moves down for non-clothing-first brands: Skechers 4->10 (footwear-first; its high spot comes from purchase-consideration polls, still kept top 10 on 4 sources); Victoria's Secret 9->18 (lingerie/beauty, people asked for clothing brands rarely start there); Louis Vuitton 13->21 (luxury leather goods first). Others shift by one or two from these moves. Dropped from raw top 24: Vans (raw 23) and Lee (raw 24), displaced by American Eagle and H&M.
confidence: medium - Top 6 (Nike, Adidas, Levi's, Old Navy, Under Armour, Hanes) are backed by all 5 sources and very solid. No free-recall poll for 'name a clothing brand' exists, so the middle (Gap, Ralph Lauren, Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger, American Eagle, H&M) was placed by gut check backed by fame and revenue; YouGov opinion data alone would rank them lower. Tail (Louis Vuitton, Converse, Reebok, Banana Republic vs Vans/Lee/Champion/Zara/Lululemon) is close and interchangeable. All three survey-type sources come from YouGov.
